subject: Post-demo probe plan: Parallax competitive tests & owners
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo probe plan: Parallax competitive tests & owners

Hi Soma — thanks again for the demo session this morning. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight probe plan so we can align on the next week: 

1) Goal: short, comparable runs to validate latency, throughput, and token-cost tradeoffs across Parallax's core QA workload. We want to show where Redwood yields cost or latency advantages and where the hyperscaler baseline still makes sense.

2) Proposed tests (owners in parens):
  - Latency p50/p95 (256-token prompts; owner: Rishi)
  - Throughput (concurrent requests, 1k/5k token totals; owner: Marissa)
  - Cost-per-1M-tokens estimate (hosted vs dedicated) (owner: Marcus)
  - Cache hit behavior / prefix-caching for repeated prompts (owner: Rishi)
  - Cold-start warm-up (container spinup and model load times) (owner: Marissa)
  - Correctness/checkpoint parity on your sample corpus (owner: Parallax — Soma)

3) Test variants:
  - Hyperscaler-managed endpoint (baseline)
  - Redwood Hosted (same model family, standard FP16)
  - Redwood Dedicated quantized run (if you want to test cost-forward option)

4) Success criteria (draft):
  - p95 latency within <= 1.5x baseline OR meaningful cost delta (>20%) in favor of Redwood for equal perf
  - No functional regressions on Parallax sample set (diff < 2% top-level intent mismatch)
  - Throughput target: sustain 60 req/s for 256-token workload during a 10-minute steady window

5) Timeline & next steps:
  - Someday this week: Parallax provides a 5k-sample subset and a small test harness (we can run directly against your dataset)
  - Wed 07/21: Redwood runs first pass and shares probe-test-matrix.xlsx with results (Marissa)
  - Fri 07/23: Sync to review results and decide on deeper dedicated runs (Marcus + Parallax)

Attachments: probe-test-matrix.xlsx (blank template) — I attached a stub with owners and the sampling plan. If this looks good, reply with confirmation and we'll schedule the Wed run.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Quick tech addendum to make the probe results comparable:

1) Model parity: run the same model family and prompt templates across all endpoints. If exact weights differ, run identical prompt/response scoring with deterministic seeds where supported.
2) Measurement windows: run three 10-minute steady-state windows per variant (warmup 2m, measure 10m). Capture p50/p95, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec, and per-request cost estimates (lambda + infra).
3) Streaming/prefix workload: implement a 30-min run that replays a 2000-item prefix-heavy stream (50% repeated prefixes). Measure effective latency delta at 50/95/99 and prefix cache hit-rate.
4) Success numbers (draft):
   - p95 for 256-token tasks: target <= 180ms (hosted) and <= 140ms (dedicated quantized) to be considered a clear latency win vs hyperscaler baseline.
   - Cost delta: >= 25% unit-cost improvement on dedicated quantized run vs hyperscaler if latency stays within 1.2x.
   - Functional parity: automated diff script must pass with <2% intent-change across test set.

I'll drop the wrapper scripts into the shared Drive and update the probe-test-matrix. Marissa — ping me if you need the container images (we'll publish a small image with our benchmarking harness).

— Rishi
